tasks.title: Add inclusive From/To calendar controls and range contract
tasks.component: Analytical filter UI and date-range utilities
tasks.objective: Replace month-only selection with an accessible explicit calendar range whose validated timezone-less SQL datetime bounds drive analytics without discovered-period restrictions.
requirements: Provide native From and To date inputs plus Apply; discovery may seed but never constrain the range.
Replace the current month-only construction and controls rooted in site/date-range.js and the dashboard selection lifecycle; do not retain 23:59:59 month bounds as the applied range path.
Accept real YYYY-MM-DD dates in years 1753 through 9999 with From not after To; invalid input issues zero requests.
Convert exactly to FromDate T00:00:00 and inclusive ToDate T23:59:59.997 without a timezone suffix.
Support one-day, cross-month/year, and out-of-discovery ranges, including empty discovery.
Keep draft edits separate and retain the applied range across refresh and fresh authorized re-entry.
Use Hebrew labels/errors, aria-invalid and useful focus; preserve keyboard use, 44px targets, RTL/LTR, and responsive fit.
Ten draft edits must initiate zero analytical or snapshot requests; the subsequent accepted Apply initiates exactly four analytical and zero snapshot requests.
acceptanceCriteria: Valid one-day and cross-year submissions expose exact inclusive bounds including .997 and no Z.
Missing, impossible, reversed, pre-1753, and post-9999 input announces an inline error, focuses an input, and produces zero API effects.
A valid range absent from discovery applies after both non-empty and empty discovery.
Controls remain labeled, keyboard operable, and overflow-free at 390x844 and 1440x900 in RTL and LTR.
At each required viewport/direction, record the accepted Apply request counts and post-response render time; render completes under 50 ms with no app-attributable task lasting 50 ms or more.
validationScenarios: Exercise leap/non-leap dates, both year bounds, reversed dates, one day, and December-to-January.
Edit without applying, refresh, then apply; verify only Apply changes requests and re-entry retains the range.
Return no periods, enter an arbitrary valid range, and verify Apply remains usable.

tasks.title: Drive analytics through one generation-bound applied range
tasks.component: Analytical data loader and XState lifecycle
tasks.objective: Load all four analytical reports concurrently with identical applied bounds and prevent stale request or authorization generations from committing.
requirements: Store selectedRange independently from periods and pass it to division, summary, category, and closure.
Separate analytical Apply/REFRESH from the coupled authorization-refresh path currently visible in site/app.js so analytics never triggers the snapshot controller.
Start exactly four concurrent analytical requests per accepted Apply or analytical refresh.
Abort superseded work and ignore stale request IDs and out-of-order authorization/apply generations.
Refresh ready/empty analytics through REFRESH; reserve RETRY for recoverable error states.
Preserve aggregation, charts, CSP, sanitization, errors, and host authorization.
Keep analytical operations isolated from the enabled three-report current snapshot.
Measure 0, 1, and 1,000 rows per report, including duplicate-heavy and malformed boundaries; record decoded bytes, warmed mapping/render time, peak concurrency, long tasks, and dashboard descendants.

Bound the 1,000-row-per-report case to 4,000 combined rows and 4 MiB decoded, warmed aggregate mapping under 100 ms, post-response render under 50 ms, no app-attributable task of 50 ms or more, and at most 600 dashboard descendants.
acceptanceCriteria: All four request bodies carry identical FromDate and ToDate for the applied range.

Ten rapid applications initiate exactly 40 analytical and zero snapshot requests with peak active analytical concurrency at most four; only the newest four may complete and commit, while the prior 36 are aborted or settle ignored.
Refresh reloads the displayed applied range in ready and empty states.
Analytics creates no extra snapshot call and changes no snapshot facts or timestamp.
Evidence records analytical initiated, aborted, completed, and committed totals plus decoded bytes, mapping/render samples, peak concurrency, descendant count, and long-task count.
validationScenarios: Resolve delayed old and new ranges out of order and verify only new data renders.
Refresh an empty result and verify four requests retain the applied range.
Observe snapshot calls, facts, and timestamp across multiple analytical applies.

tasks.title: Normalize snapshot aggregate strings and bound recovery guidance
tasks.component: Current snapshot adapters, lifecycle, and error UI
tasks.objective: Accept legitimate decimal-string event/permit aggregates without weakening invariants and present report-specific recovery guidance without disclosing untrusted content.
requirements: Normalize safe non-negative integer numbers and trimmed digit-only strings for event/permit aggregate fields.
Replace only the number-only field guard currently used by site/current-snapshot.js event/permit adapters; retain numeric envelope TotalCount and equipment population behavior.
Keep envelope TotalCount numeric, equipment unchanged, and all reconciliation, distinct permit, required-date, and no-fabrication invariants.
Reject missing, empty, signed, fractional, exponent, negative, unsafe, malformed, and unreconciled values.
Preserve dataset and bounded HTTP status/error class through invalidation and show report-specific Hebrew guidance.
Expose only fixed endpoint paths and bounded classifications; never body text, arbitrary errors, API addresses, markers, tokens, or credentials.
Retain stale last-good facts and disable retry for 401/403/revocation until fresh re-entry; ordinary failures remain retryable.
Keep CURRENT_SNAPSHOT_LIVE_CALLS_ENABLED true and exactly three concurrent calls per snapshot load/refresh.
Measure 0, 1, 1,000, and 10,000 equipment rows with valid aggregate fixtures; record decoded bytes, warmed mapping/render time, peak concurrency, long tasks, and snapshot descendants.

Bound the 10,000-row snapshot to 2.5 MiB decoded, warmed mapping under 100 ms, render under 50 ms, no app-attributable task of 50 ms or more, and at most 80 snapshot descendants at both viewports/directions.
acceptanceCriteria: HTTP 200 with numeric envelope counts and decimal-string event/permit aggregates renders correct numeric, separately categorized facts.
Malformed/unsafe variants fail without fabricated values or partial commit.
Known failures identify the report and expose only fixed endpoint/status diagnostics; private response data never reaches DOM/logs.
401/403 after good data retains stale facts, disables retry, issues no old-generation effect, and recovers only after fresh verified re-entry.

Ten refresh/retry activations while pending coalesce to exactly three initiated requests, peak concurrency three, and one commit; after terminal denial the same burst initiates zero until fresh re-entry.
Very long digit strings and 9007199254740992 reject without partial render or nonlinear work.
validationScenarios: Test whitespace/leading-zero strings, then empty, signed, decimal, exponent, unsafe, and negative values.
Simulate equipment 500, permit 403, network, invalid response, and initial failure; verify copy, retry, diagnostics, and rendering.
Burst refresh/retry while pending; verify one bounded three-request chain and no disabled-flag regression.

tasks.title: Add a truthful all-state release footer
tasks.component: Shared document shell and packaged release metadata assets
tasks.objective: Expose Version, Last update, and Release date in one accessible responsive footer that remains visible in every application state and renders only trusted controller-stamped metadata.
requirements: Copy the builder skill's packaged release-footer.js and release-footer.css unchanged into site/assets and load them from relative same-origin paths.
Place exactly one packaged footer[data-simplyvibe-release] with its semantic dl and data-release-label/data-release-value hooks outside state-dependent main content in site/index.html.
Keep the footer in normal document flow and visible during host waiting, loading, no-context, empty, error, stale, and ready states.
Render localized Hebrew/English Version, Last update, and Release date labels and values based on document language, preserving bdi isolation and RTL/LTR behavior.
Treat missing or malformed metadata as Unavailable; previews explicitly identify Preview and show Not released; only valid production stamps show a release date.
Accept only a 12-character lowercase hexadecimal releaseVersion and valid UTC timestamps; format timestamps in the viewer timezone without using viewer current time.

Reserve stamping for the trusted controller workflow: Git version, latest site-source commit time, and frozen production publication time must never be inferred from data refresh, event, page-open, or hand-maintained values.
Make no footer network or authentication request and include no user, tenant, token, credential, or controller-internal metadata.
Keep the release footer visually distinct from data-refresh timestamps, responsive without overlap or horizontal overflow at 390x844 and 1440x900, and accessible under zoom in RTL and LTR.
acceptanceCriteria: Every runtime state retains one visible footer with all three labels and values; state transitions never remove or duplicate it.
Unstamped and invalid synthetic metadata render localized Unavailable values and never synthesize a timestamp or version.
Synthetic preview metadata renders the validated 12-character version with an explicit Preview label, valid Last update, and Not released for Release date.
Synthetic production metadata renders the validated version and both valid frozen timestamps; changing document language relocalizes labels and values.
At both required viewports and directions the footer remains in flow, wraps without horizontal overflow or content obstruction, and remains distinguishable from dashboard last-refresh copy.
Static and browser evidence records exactly one footer marker, same-origin asset loads, zero footer fetch/auth calls, and the absence of sensitive metadata.
validationScenarios: Render host-waiting/loading, missing-context, empty, recoverable error, terminal authorization error with stale data, and ready states; assert the same single footer remains visible.
Exercise absent attributes, malformed version/timestamps, valid preview attributes with empty release time, and valid production attributes using explicit local synthetic fixtures.
Switch html lang and dir between Hebrew RTL and English LTR, resize to 390x844 and 1440x900, and inspect wrapping, bdi isolation, labels, values, and overflow.
Instrument fetch and host-command paths while rendering and changing language; assert the footer initiates no request or authentication operation.
